summary: Salmon National Forest lookout in Idaho County: a 60-foot pole tower dated 1941, ordered burned in 1967 and listed as gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as Gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association and firelookout.com; the 1967 burn order is the only fate the pages describe.

visit.trail_note: Tagged Hike-In on idahofirelookouts.com; no trail details given.

events.note: 60-foot pole tower with log cabin; a September 1940 newspaper item had it under construction
Orders to burn the lookout carried out in the fall

evidence.supports: September 1940 newspaper item: tower under construction on the point
evidence.quote: A new timber lookout tower is under construction on Nolan Point which is situated on the high breaks west of the mouth of the Middlefork.

evidence.supports: 1941 date; 60-foot pole tower with log cabin; gone
orders to burn carried out in the fall of 1967
evidence.quote: 1967: The orders to burn the lookout were carried out in the Fall.

evidence.supports: hike-in access tag; listed as gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A September 1940 Recorder Herald item, quoted on Forest Lookouts, has the tower under construction; firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts date it to 1941. No source gives a finish date, so the story gives 1941 as the recorded year and notes the 1940 report.

notes_for_editor: Only two pages give the 1941 build date, 60-foot size and burn order, and the 1940 newspaper item is quoted only through Forest Lookouts; I did not check it against the newspaper. idahofirelookouts.com also gives 1941 and 60 feet but its text uses typographic characters, so it is not quoted for those facts. Its page says no staffing history is documented, so staffing is left out. The record's height was null; 60 feet is now 18.3 m. The 8,215-foot elevation appears in the story but is not a facts key. A web search found no independent source; one search snippet suggested a different forest for these Idaho County lookouts, but it was unverified and not used.
